argenx Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update
Continued strong VYVGART performance drives $1.7 billion in global product net sales, representing 54% year-over-year growth and 13% quarter-over-quarter growth

sBLA for VYVGART Hytrulo in IMNM on track for submission by year-end; pursuing additional registrational study in DM

Phase 3 MMN data for empasiprubart expected in December 2026

FB102 advancing to Phase 3 in celiac disease as potential new growth pillar in argenx’s next wave of immunology innovation

Management to host conference call today at 2:30 PM CET (8:30 AM ET)

October 22, 2026 7:00 AM CET

Amsterdam, the Netherlands – argenx SE (Euronext & Nasdaq: ARGX), the immunology innovation company, today announced its third quarter 2026 results and provided a business update.

“The story of argenx is one of continued innovation, growth and impact,” said Karen Massey, Chief Executive Officer. “VYVGART is the foundation of our business and continues to deliver strong performance across gMG and CIDP, with significant opportunity still ahead as we reach more patients, expand into new indications, and advance the next wave of FcRn medicines. The positive results from our Phase 3 ALKIVIA study further reinforce the potential of VYVGART beyond neurology, and underscore how much more it can deliver for patients. The upcoming Phase 3 readout for empasiprubart in MMN, the advancement of FB102, and progress across our emerging immunology pipeline are bringing the next chapter of argenx into focus as we build a global immunology innovator positioned for durable growth and value creation well beyond Vision 2030.”

Vision 2030

argenx remains on track to achieve its ‘Vision 2030’ anchored in the ambition to treat 50,000 patients globally with its medicines, secure 10 labeled indications, and progress five pipeline candidates into registrational development by 2030.

Realizing the full potential of VYVGART and advancing FcRn leadership

VYVGART® (IV: efgartigimod alfa-fcab; SC: efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc) is the first-and-only approved treatment for all adult patients living with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG). It is also approved for chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) globally, and primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in Japan. Building on VYVGART’s leadership in MG and CIDP, argenx is progressing multiple label and indication expansions, exploring VYVGART’s potential in additional autoimmune diseases through proof-of-concept studies, and advancing next-generation FcRn molecules and delivery modalities.
•Generated $1.7 billion in global product net sales in the third quarter of 2026, representing 54% year-over-year growth and 13% quarter-over-quarter growth
•Submitted a Supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for VYVGART in ocular myasthenia gravis (oMG) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
•sBLA for VYVGART and VYVGART Hytrulo in pediatric gMG accepted for priority review by the FDA, with a PDUFA target action date in February 2027
•VYVGART Hytrulo autoinjector expected to launch in second half of 2027 for all approved indications
•Reported positive Phase 3 ALKIVIA results with consistent and clinically meaningful treatment effects observed across immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) and dermatomyositis (DM); sBLA for VYVGART Hytrulo in IMNM on track for submission by year-end 2026, supported by Breakthrough Therapy Designation, with plans to conduct an additional registrational study in DM.
•Topline results from Phase 3 ADVANCE-NEXT study in primary ITP expected in first half of 2027
•Phase 3 VitaliThy studies in Graves’ disease ongoing;
•Advancing the future FcRn portfolio, including Phase 3-ready ARGX-213, designed for monthly dosing, and ARGX-124 currently in Phase 1 development


Advancing empasiprubart, argenx’s second pipeline-in-a-product opportunity

Empasiprubart (anti-C2) is argenx’s second pipeline-in-a-product opportunity and is being evaluated in Phase 3 studies in multifocal motor neuropathy (MMN) and CIDP, with additional Phase 2 studies exploring its potential in other indications and in combination with VYVGART in gMG.

•Topline results from the Phase 3 EMPASSION study (MMN) expected in December 2026
•Topline results from Phase 3 EMVIGORATE and EMNERGIZE studies in CIDP anticipated in the second half of 2027
•Phase 2 ADAPT-Forward platform study in gMG ongoing, evaluating empasiprubart as an add-on to efgartigimod and as monotherapy to support combination development pathway

Delivering next wave of immunology innovation

Beyond the FcRn portfolio and empasiprubart, argenx is advancing a differentiated immunology pipeline that includes FB102 (CD122), adimanebart (MuSK), ARGX-121 (IgA), ARGX-109 (IL-6), TSP-101 (Fn14), ARGX-118 (Galectin-10) and ARGX-125 (undisclosed target), together with additional candidates emerging from the Immunology Innovation Program. These programs support argenx’s ambition to build multiple pillars of sustainable growth beyond Vision 2030.

•Advancing FB102 to Phase 3 in celiac disease based on positive Phase 2 results, with ongoing programs in alopecia areata and vitiligo and potential across other autoimmune diseases
•Phase 3 study of adimanebart in congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS) expected to begin in 2026; Phase 2 in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) ongoing
•Phase 2 study of ARGX-121 in IgA nephropathy (IgAN) ongoing
•Advancing Phase 1 development of TSP-101, ARGX-118 and ARGX-125

DETAILS OF THE FINANCIAL RESULTS
Total operating income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.8 billion and $4.6 billion, respectively, compared to $1.2 billion and $2.9 billion, respectively, for the same periods in 2025, and mainly consisted of:
•Product net sales of VYVGART for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $1.7 billion and $4.5 billion, respectively, compared to $1.1 billion and $2.9 billion, respectively, for the same periods in 2025.

•Other operating income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $30 million and $71 million, respectively, compared to $24 million and $60 million, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. The other operating income in these periods primarily related to research and development tax incentives and payroll tax rebates.
Total operating expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $1.3 billion and $3.2 billion, respectively, compared to $0.8 billion and $2.2 billion, respectively, for the same periods in 2025, and mainly consisted of:
•Cost of sales for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $165 million and $431 million, respectively, compared to $109 million and $301 million, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. The cost of sales was related to the sale of VYVGART.

•Research and development expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $0.5 billion and $1.4 billion, respectively, compared to $0.4 billion and $1.0 billion, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. The research and development expenses mainly related to advancing efgartigimod, empasiprubart, adimanebart and FB102 across multiple registrational studies, plus early-stage pipeline and preclinical programs.
•Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $0.6 billion and $1.4 billion, respectively, compared to $0.3 billion and $0.9 billion, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. The selling, general and administrative expenses mainly related to professional and marketing fees linked to the global commercialization of the VYVGART franchise, and personnel expenses. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026 included approximately $150 million of acquisition-related expenses associated with the Company’s acquisition of Forte Biosciences Inc.
Financial income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $45 million and $137 million, respectively, compared to $43 million and $118 million, respectively, for the same periods in 2025.
Exchange gains/losses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were an $8 million gain and an $11 million loss, respectively, compared to a $2 million loss and a $74 million gain, respectively, for the same periods in 2025.

FULL YEAR EXPECTATIONS

Combined R&D and SG&A expenses are now expected to be approximately $4 billion for 2026, including the Forte transaction-related costs.

About VYVGART

VYVGART® (efgartigimod alfa fcab) is a first-in-class human IgG1 antibody fragment that binds to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), resulting in the reduction of circulating IgG autoantibodies. VYVGART Hytrulo® is a subcutaneous combination of efgartigimod alfa (VYVGART) and recombinant human hyaluronidase PH20 (rHuPH20), Halozyme’s ENHANZE® drug delivery technology to facilitate subcutaneous injection delivery of biologics. VYVGART is approved for generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) and immune thrombocytopenia (Japan only). VYVGART Hytrulo is approved for gMG and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP). VYVGART Hytrulo may be marketed under different proprietary names in other regions.

About argenx

argenx is the immunology innovation company, focused on turning immunology breakthroughs into medicines for patients. The company seeks novel biology wherever it emerges, co-creating with academic researchers through its Immunology Innovation Program (IIP) and investing in promising science, to develop treatments for people living with underserved diseases. By advancing molecules with the potential to reach multiple diseases and patient populations, argenx is building a world-class portfolio. This approach produced the first approved antibody fragment targeting the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) and today powers a growing pipeline of early and late-stage programs across several therapeutic areas. For more information, visit www.argenx.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube.
